headline: 10 killed as fire guts Cox's Bazar resort, DU and Jagannath university students among dead
summary: The Tup-Tup Resto and Resort in Inani lacked a fire safety license, according to the Fire Service, as families and tourists were trapped in the blaze.
details: A devastating fire at the Tup-Tup Resto and Resort near Patuartek beach in Inani, Ukhiya, has left at least 10 people dead, including a Dhaka University student and a Jagannath University student.
The blaze broke out around 6:30 am on Saturday, catching guests and tourists by surprise. Two units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence brought the flames under control by 8:15 am.
Survivors recount harrowing experiences, such as Ashiqul Islam, who escaped by breaking a window and jumping out, but was unable to save his wife and five other relatives who remain missing.
Cox's Bazar Deputy Commissioner A Mannan is overseeing the identification of recovered bodies through DNA sampling to ensure they are matched with the missing relatives.
The Fire Service has revealed that the resort operated without a valid fire safety license, raising serious questions about the safety of tourists in the region.
The victims included several members of a single family from Dhaka, highlighting the tragedy of a vacation trip that turned into a nightmare.
caption:
A family vacation turned into a nightmare as 10 people died in a resort fire in Cox's Bazar.

A devastating fire at the Tup-Tup Resto and Resort near Patuartek beach in Inani, Ukhiya, has left at least 10 people dead, including a Dhaka University student and a Jagannath University student.

The blaze broke out around 6:30 am on Saturday, catching guests and tourists by surprise. Two units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence brought the flames under control by 8:15 am.

Survivors recount harrowing experiences, such as Ashiqul Islam, who escaped by breaking a window and jumping out, but was unable to save his wife and five other relatives who remain missing.

Cox's Bazar Deputy Commissioner A Mannan is overseeing the identification of recovered bodies through DNA sampling to ensure they are matched with the missing relatives.

The Fire Service has revealed that the resort operated without a valid fire safety license, raising serious questions about the safety of tourists in the region.

The victims included several members of a single family from Dhaka, highlighting the tragedy of a vacation trip that turned into a nightmare.

headline_marked: Minister Ishraque [[wields pistol in anti-drug raid]] in Gendaria
headline: Minister Ishraque wields pistol in anti-drug raid in Gendaria
summary: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain chased suspects with a firearm, sparking online debate over the legality of his actions.
details: State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain was seen in a video chasing a group of people with a pistol and a loudspeaker in Gendaria, Dhaka.
The minister jumped out of a vehicle, pointed the weapon at suspects, and shouted for them to stop during what he described as an operation to demolish a drug den.
Gendaria Police confirmed that six people were collected and handed over to them, with some powder found on the suspects that is currently being tested.
Police officials stated that the state minister did not inform them beforehand about the operation, learning about the incident only after the suspects were detained.
The footage, posted on Ishraque's Facebook page, drew mixed reactions online, with some questioning the legality of a minister using a firearm openly.
Others defended the action, arguing that a licensed firearm could be used in such a manner, while some compared the minister to a fictional action hero.
In a subsequent post, Ishraque vowed to continue anti-drug operations until Dhaka-6 is drug-free, regardless of the political affiliation of the traders.
caption:
A State Minister with a pistol in hand chasing suspects through the streets of Gendaria. Is this law enforcement or a movie scene?

State Minister for Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain was seen in a video chasing a group of people with a pistol and a loudspeaker in Gendaria, Dhaka.

The minister jumped out of a vehicle, pointed the weapon at suspects, and shouted for them to stop during what he described as an operation to demolish a drug den.

Gendaria Police confirmed that six people were collected and handed over to them, with some powder found on the suspects that is currently being tested.

Police officials stated that the state minister did not inform them beforehand about the operation, learning about the incident only after the suspects were detained.

The footage, posted on Ishraque's Facebook page, drew mixed reactions online, with some questioning the legality of a minister using a firearm openly.

Others defended the action, arguing that a licensed firearm could be used in such a manner, while some compared the minister to a fictional action hero.

In a subsequent post, Ishraque vowed to continue anti-drug operations until Dhaka-6 is drug-free, regardless of the political affiliation of the traders.
